question: Plasma membrane of cell is bounded to cytoskeleton by which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Plasma membrane" -> "contains integral and peripheral proteins" -> "Ankyrin" -> "binds integral proteins to spectrin" -> "spectrin links to actin filaments of cytoskeleton" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Plasma membrane" -> "structural support needed" -> "Spectrin" -> "forms mesh under cell membrane" -> "supports cell shape" -> "not directly involved in binding to cytoskeleton" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Plasma membrane" -> "interaction with cytoskeleton" -> "Tubulin" -> "primary component of microtubules" -> "microtubules support cell shape" -> "not directly involved in plasma membrane binding" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Plasma membrane" -> "requires attachment to cytoskeleton for stability" -> "Laminin" -> "part of extracellular matrix" -> "does not bind directly to cytoskeleton within the context of plasma membrane" -> 50%
analysis: Ankyrin is the correct answer as it directly binds integral proteins of the plasma membrane to the spectrin network, thus linking the plasma membrane to the cytoskeleton. This role is crucial for the structural integrity and function of the cell, and is well-supported by standard medical knowledge.
